questions.q: Per this lesson, why isn't the original pilot business case from Data Governance Foundations enough to keep a program funded long-term?
options: It is identical to a value realization report, so nothing else is needed
It was never approved in the first place
Business cases automatically renew themselves with no further action
It was written to win one first yes for a scoped pilot, not to renew funding every budget cycle afterward
questions.explain: The first business case's whole job is winning the initial pilot funding; sustaining funding requires a different, recurring justification.

questions.q: What is a 'run-rate budget' as described in this lesson?
options: An ongoing operating budget line for governance, renewed like payroll rather than re-pitched as a new project each cycle
A one-time grant that expires automatically after the pilot
A budget that only covers the program's first ninety days
A budget that requires no owner or cost center
questions.explain: Converting from a project budget to a run-rate budget means the program is renewed as standing operations, not re-pitched from scratch.

questions.q: What three things does a value realization report need to show, per this lesson?
options: A brand-new, unrelated business case for a different initiative
Value delivered against the original promise, the cost of not having the program, and what's different this cycle
A list of every employee's name on the governance council
Only the original pilot's anticipated value, repeated unchanged
questions.explain: These three elements, built from existing KPIs, are what let a sustaining program prove its existing budget already paid off.

questions.q: How does the roadmap's now/next/later structure (Lesson 21) help when a budget gets cut, per this lesson?
options: It has no relationship to budget conversations at all
It requires canceling every committed 'Now' item automatically
It guarantees the budget can never be cut
It lets the program name precisely what stays, what slips, and what waits, instead of the whole program collapsing
questions.explain: Because the backlog is already sorted by horizon and priority, a cut can be absorbed precisely rather than catastrophically.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend to protect a program's funding when a sponsoring champion leaves?
options: Relying entirely on one remaining person's personal memory of why the program mattered
Waiting until the champion leaves to start building other relationships
Immediately dissolving the governance council
Spreading sponsorship and communication across the council and multiple stakeholders before it's tested
questions.explain: The lesson ties this back to Chapter 4's discipline of spreading sponsorship across multiple stakeholders in advance, not during a crisis.
